question: Does the already-supported higher-order within-taxon spatial coherence persist when observer identity and physical SiteID are simultaneously held constant?
sample: Intersection of same-observer matched pairs and pairs retaining identical nonmissing SiteID at all ten StopNumbers.
endpoint: Exactly the previously frozen higher_order_within_species_mass = sum choose(max(k-1,0),2) across route-new taxa, with no redefinition.
conditioning: Exactly the previously frozen null-regression conditioning on route_new_species_gain beta and extra_stop_incidence_gain beta.
nulls: uniform activation kappa=2 re-estimated within the restricted sample
persistence-preserving activation anchor=0.75 re-estimated within the restricted sample
pass_rule: Joint robustness passes only if the observed higher-order conditional residual exceeds the upper 95% residual bound under both null families.
interpretation: A pass shows the higher-order coherence does not require observer turnover or physical-stop relocation.
The test remains post-freeze and does not establish literal synchrony, movement, hydrological connectivity, or causal rainfall.
No metric, conditioning covariate, null family, tail, or threshold may change after endpoint readback.
